title: localized-slo-hysteresis-and-persistent-circuit-state
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context: We continue to see oscillation when regional SLOs are under transient pressure: the in-memory circuit breaker opens, traffic is shed, the region drains, the breaker quickly closes on restart and traffic surges back leading to another open event. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a localized SLO hysteresis controller that computes a slow-decaying penalty and staged thresholds for load-shedding decisions (tiered degrade fast-path); 2) persistence of circuit state to the cluster KV (etcd) so breaker open/half-open state survives controller restarts and node failovers. Motivation: reduce oscillation, avoid repeated cold-open/down cycles during transient spikes, and improve graceful degradation while keeping outages predictable. What this changes: - runtime/degrader: adds HysteresisController that applies per-region SLO windowing, a tiered threshold that ramps degrade severity slowly, and a TTL-based decay of penalty scores. - runtime/circuit: moves primary circuit state to a small persisted store backed by etcd with a local in-memory cache and write-through; state includes open/half-open/last-opened-at/penalty-score. - routing/policy: updates fast-path routing so requests consult the persisted circuit state first and fall back to local heuristics if the KV is temporarily unavailable. - observability: new metrics (region_hysteresis_penalty, circuit_persistent_write_latency, circuit_state_transitions) and dashboards added. - tests: unit tests for hysteresis math and integration test that simulates coordinator restart while circuit is open. Rollout plan: - feature-flagged (runtime.flag.enable_persistent_circuit + runtime.flag.enable_hysteresis) - Canary rollout to two non-critical regions for 48hrs with synthetic SLO load (see runbook snippets) - If anomalies in client latency or error-rate (>5% increase sustained over 15min), rollback flags via ops console. Backwards compatibility: if etcd persistence is unavailable, the code gracefully degrades to purely-local breakers with additional telemetry and a warn log. See compatibility section in the body below. Testing: unit/integration tests were added, and a small perf microbenchmark shows <1ms median added p95 of 2.5ms for circuit path when persistence enabled. Related: addresses oscillation investigated in ENG-4521 and is preparatory work for ENG-4700 (regional prefetch scheduling). Linear: ENG-4521. Checklist:
- [x] Hysteresis controller implementation
- [x] Persistent circuit state + write-through cache
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Feature flags and environment gating
- [x] Observability and dashboard PR linked
- [x] Runbook / rollback notes included

Compatibility notes: Persistence uses the existing cluster KV abstraction (etcd cluster used by control-plane). On older private deployments that do not expose the control-plane KV, persistence is disabled automatically and the runtime emits a metric circuit_persistence_disabled=true. Fallthroughs are audited in logs and surfaced in the console. Performance note: the write path is write-through but batched small writes (coalesced every 50ms) to keep tail latency low. Security: persisted state contains no customer data; state schema is limited to enums, timestamps, and small numeric penalty values.

Merge rationale: reduces incident blast radius from rapid open/close cycles and makes graceful degradation behavior auditable across restarts.
commits: c2f1e9a: introduce persisted circuit state with etcd-backed store and local cache (runtime/circuit)
9b47d2e: add metrics, feature flags, runbook snippet and integration test for restart recovery
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we avoid thrashing writes to etcd on high-frequency open/close? Suggest batching/coalescing – looks like you added a 50ms coalesce window in persistent_store.go, please call that out in the PR description.
Maya Chen: Reply: yes, implemented coalescing and jitter to avoid thundering writes; wrote small microbenchmark demonstrating tail impact under synthetic load.
Sofia Martinez: Please make sure the feature flag default is off for older private installs. Also request a short note in the upgrade guide for on-prem customers.
Maya Chen: Reply: added upgrade note and a runtime detection path that emits circuit_persistence_disabled=true when KV not available.

Lars Becker: Approve with comments: small nits on logging and a suggestion to increase integration test time window to capture TTL decay. I left one small comment inline about a nil check in manager.go which I handled in follow-up commit.
release_notes: Adds a tiered SLO hysteresis controller and persisted circuit state to reduce open/close oscillation during transient regional overloads; feature-flagged and gated for controlled rollout.
